# Work in Gavana

This is optional help for any Gavana request. It adds no steps: a simple
request goes straight to the tool that does it.

## The person's words win

- Do what the person asked, in their words. Their count, references and roles,
  composition, aspect ratio, on-image text, language, destination and
  exclusions override any guide default or example, including this one.
- Take the shortest supported path. Reading a canvas, saving an image, one edit
  or one image needs no guide, no campaign planning and no workflow.
- Do not widen the task. One image is not a campaign; "change the background"
  is not permission to change the product.

## Canvas basics

- Use the canvas the person points at, or find it with `canvas_list` (follow
  `page.nextCursor` for later pages). With no canvas in the
  chat, ask which canvas; call `canvas_create` only when the person asks for a
  new one, and reuse its `canvas.handle` for every later read, save and
  generation in the task. Never create a canvas per operation.
- Call `canvas_get` before changing an existing canvas (`detail: "summary"`
  first on a large board). Keep unrelated nodes, positions and connections.
- `canvas_get` and `canvas_create` return `url`, the verified link to give the
  person.
- For several node changes, check them with `canvas_validate`, apply one
  `canvas_apply_batch` with the current revision, then validate again.

## Save references before using them

- A picture the person gave you is not on the canvas yet. Save it with
  `save_image_to_canvas` and use the `node:` handle it returns.
- Pass every reference to generation with the role it plays: `identity` for
  what must stay exact, and `construction`, `texture`, `fit` or `style` for
  what to borrow. Never reduce a reference to a description in the prompt.
- A product page is a source, not prompt text: pass it to `save_image_to_canvas`
  as `productPageUrl`, then use the `node:` handles it returns as references.
  "Make photos from this page" means generating new images from those
  references; the imported photos are not the deliverable.
  A `review_required` answer wrote nothing; pass the variant or the exact
  `imageUrls` it asks for. Until an import succeeds, do not generate that
  product: a prompt alone draws a lookalike.

## Count versus distinct directions

- `count` (1-4) makes that many separate images of one prompt.
- Different subjects, scenes, hooks or ratios are one `generate_image_in_canvas` call
  with `items`: one item per output (1-4), each with its own `prompt`, and an
  `aspectRatio` or `label` when that output needs one. References, model and
  destination apply to every item. Never fold them into one prompt with
  `count`. The result lists one run per item in `runs`; `nextAction` names the
  first unfinished one, and each needs checking.
- "4 scenes of this bag" is four items sharing the bag's `node:` reference.
  "The same ad in 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9" is three items, one ratio each.
- A comparison, grid or collage inside one image is `composition`, not `count`.
- To change an existing image, call `generate_image_in_canvas` with
  `operation: "edit"` and pass
  the image being edited as `source` (a `node:` or `asset:` handle). Gavana
  sends it to the model first, as Image 1. `references` are extra guidance
  (identity, style, construction), not the image being edited. A new output is
  created and the source stays.
- To limit an edit to part of the image, add `changeRegions`: up to eight
  `{ x, y, width, height }` rectangles, each 0-1 of the image and inside it.
  Only those areas may change; Gavana keeps the source's pixels everywhere
  else. It needs a declared source, either `source` or a reference with
  `role: "source"`.

## Ratio, on-image text and language

- Carry the requested aspect ratio as `requirements.aspectRatio`, for example
  `"9:16"`, or as each item's `aspectRatio` when outputs differ.
  Writing the ratio only into the prompt does not set it.
- "No text" is `requirements.text: "none"`. Exact copy is `requirements.copy`
  with `text: "specified"`, spelled as the person wrote it.
- Record the language on-image copy must use in `requirements.language`. Do
  not translate copy the person supplied.
- Keep the person's full request in `originalWording`.

## Spend only with authorization

- Generation can cost the person money. Start it only when they asked for it
  in this conversation. Reading, saving and validating need no permission.
- Never retry a failed generation on your own. Reuse an `idempotencyKey` only
  to repeat the identical request.
- A direct request to make, generate or edit images or video is the permission
  for that one job: do it, even while another run is pending. "Gen thêm 1 cái"
  or "one more" is a new direct request: do it with a new `idempotencyKey`.
- A plain yes ("yes", "ừ", "ok") to your own offer to regenerate authorizes
  that one regeneration. A repeated or ambiguous message ("làm lại?", the same
  request again) is not a yes: report what already exists and any problem you
  saw, and ask. A complaint alone ("xấu quá") is not a request either; say what
  you would change and ask once.
- Generation returns queued progress: report it. To check it, call the tool
  and arguments in the returned `nextAction`; image runs and video jobs are
  checked by different tools, so never reuse one kind's status tool for the
  other. Never start another generation to find out.
- A model the person named must be the one used. Find its handle with
  `model_list`, using a video capability for video. If it is not available,
  say so.

## Report limitations instead of substituting

- When a requirement cannot be met, because a model, ratio, count, reference or
  capability is missing, say which one and why. Do not quietly swap in
  something close, drop a reference, or claim the task is done.
- Claim an image done only when its outputs exist on the canvas and, after a
  batch edit, `canvas_validate`, with `expectedOutputNodeIds` set to the image/video node handles this
  task produced (pass other edited nodes as `nodeIds`), reports `completionReview.doneClaimAllowed: true`. A finished video is a protected link in the job's result; it is not
  added to the canvas, so give the person that link and do not look for it on
  the board.
